content: Welcome to Tweetbook. Tweetbook was created with the goal of preserving and sharing intriguing peer-reviewed case reports in interventional cardiology. The platform aims to foster productive discussions about these cases by leveraging the enthusiasm and engagement of the Twitter cardiology community. We are specifically seeking case reports that pertain to interventional cardiology. Authors are encouraged to carefully review and adhere to the following submission guidelines to ensure a more efficient response time. Case reports that include imaging studies or pictures demonstrating either significant classic findings, novel discoveries, or techniques will be considered for publication. Submissions that provide insights into fundamental mechanisms, emphasize abnormalities, or highlight potential new techniques or applications for noninvasive interventions are also welcome. Once a case is published, it will be shared on Twitter to stimulate discussion among the authors and the broader Twitter audience. Authors are encouraged to actively participate in this interactive process. For submissions to Tweetbook, the written portion of the case should include a title page and a descriptive text that does not exceed two double-spaced pages. The text should be written in 12-point Times New Roman font and may include up to five references and a multimedia legend. Motion clips can be submitted in GIF format, while images should be in JPEG, PNG, or TIFF format. Other media formats will not be accepted.
